feedback.problem: Consider the positive infinite geometric sequence that has a first term equal to $9$ and a third term equal to $4.$ What is the sum to infinity of the terms of this sequence?
feedback.worked_solution:
The sum to infinity ${S}_{\infty }$ of a geometric series is given by the formula

$$
{S}_{\infty }=\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r},\,|r|<1,
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term and $r$ is the common ratio.

From the question statement we have ${a}_{1}=9$ and ${a}_{3}=4.$ We can find the common ratio using the following formula:

$$
{r}^{n-m}=\frac{{a}_{n}}{{a}_{m}}
$$

Substituting in the known information into the above gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{3-1} & =\frac{4}{9} \\ {r}^{2} & =\frac{4}{9} \\ {r}^{2} & ={(\frac{2}{3})}^{2} \\ r & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we have taken the positive square root since we're told that the sequence is positive.

So, using the formula, we find that the sum to infinity is

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{\infty } & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{9}{(1-\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =\frac{9}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =9\cdot 3 \\  & =27.\end{aligned}
$$
